intended_object: For a smooth, proper, geometrically connected family of curves f : X → S and a scheme T over S, this is Pic⁰_{X/S}(T): the subgroup of the relative Picard group Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) made of the classes whose restriction to every geometric fibre has degree zero. The intended object comes from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud §8.4 and Kleiman §9.5.
explanation:
The body takes `relativePicardDegreeZeroSubfunctor f` at T as its carrier set. That set consists of the classes c in Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) such that, for every algebraically closed field Ω (in the universe u) and every point ξ : Spec Ω → T, the fibre degree of c at ξ is 0.

**How the fibre degree is defined.** It is `LineBundleClass.eulerDegree`, namely χ(L|_{X_ξ}) − χ(𝒪_{X_ξ}), computed over Ω on the fibre X_ξ = Spec Ω ×_S X, with χ truncated as h⁰ − h¹.

**Why this is the usual degree.** Under the section's hypotheses (proper, smooth of relative dimension 1, geometrically connected), every geometric fibre is a smooth, proper, connected curve. On such a curve, χ(L) − χ(𝒪) is the usual degree by Riemann–Roch, so the condition is the textbook one: degree zero on every geometric fibre.

**Remaining checks.**
- The fibre degree is well defined on the quotient by Pic(T), because line bundles on Spec Ω are trivial.
- Restricting Ω to algebraically closed fields in universe u loses nothing: every point of T has an algebraic closure of its residue field in that universe.
- Closure under products and inverses is proved from additivity of the degree on smooth curves. That additivity is the reason the smooth, proper, geometrically connected hypotheses are needed: they are what make this set a subgroup. This is the standard setting in which Pic⁰ of a family of curves is defined this way, so the definition is not too narrow.
- The relative Picard presheaf is defined as Pic(X_T) modulo the image of Pic(T), as the docstring states.

Mathlib has no relative Picard functor and no Pic⁰.
